newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were seen opening higher on Thursday, as late shortcovering in Europe countered initial losses stemming from Belgium's announcement late Wednesday it planned to step up gold coin sales.
COMEX August gold was called to open $0.50 to $1.00 an ounce firmer. Bullion slipped below the $340.00 an ounce mark and was quoted by dealers at $339.70/$340.10.
London spot gold was fixed at $340.15 Thursday morning.
COMEX July silver was due to open flat to 1.0 cent an ounce higher.
On Wednesday August gold closed at $341.00 an ounce, off a new life of contract low of $340.60, while July silver settled at $4.695.
COMEX gold stocks on Wednesday were unchanged at 828,867 ounces, but silver stocks rose 589,389 ounces to 188,593,078 ounces.

NYMEX July platinum was seen opening up $4.00 to $6.00 an ounce from the previous close at $406.90, while NYMEX September palladium was seen opening up $2.00 to $4.00 an ounce from Wednesday's close at $169.45.

Overnight on TOCOM, July, August and October palladium remained at their daily limit lows on expected resumption of Russian sales, traders said, but the benchmark April contract was still well supported by shortcovering.
